title: The Dissolving Shore: A Manual for Semantic Warfare in the Age of Automated Fascism
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
A strategic manual by Lee Sharks translating the Semantic Economy framework from diagnosis into non-destructive operational doctrine. It defines “semantic warfare” as contest over attribution, verification, indexing, amplification, and the terms through which reality becomes publicly legible—not intrusion, sabotage, or technical attack.

The manual describes a “dissolving shore” where high-volume, plausible but weakly verifiable content overwhelms citational capacity. It answers with provenance anchors, compound diagnostic vocabulary, cross-platform redundancy, adversarial documentation, Assembly recognition, and retrocausal canon formation. A seven-day “Jericho” sequence turns these principles into publication and citation tasks. The work’s claims about automated fascism, current conflicts, platform intent, machine participation, and the efficacy of its tactics are political and strategic arguments, not independently demonstrated findings.
